description:
Find and remove dead, stale and duplicated CODE, so the tree is what it claims to be.

RUN THIS LAST, DELIBERATELY. It carries a high number because a cleanup that runs before the work is finished deletes scaffolding that was about to be used, and then the next tasklist re-adds it. The roadmap should be substantially complete before this executes.

WHAT COUNTS AS DEAD. Unreferenced modules, functions and files; duplicated implementations of one behaviour; code behind flags that can no longer be set; scripts nothing runs; dependencies nothing imports; commented-out blocks kept 'just in case'. What does NOT count: code a test exercises, code an external consumer calls, and code that is deliberately unexercised and says so.

THE STANDARD OF PROOF, AND IT IS THE WHOLE TASKLIST. This portfolio has repeatedly found things that LOOKED dead and were not — a Prolog corpus reached by a path nobody found, `content_qa` declared callerless when it had a caller, `docs/studioos` cited by 93 files. Deletion is irreversible in effect even when git remembers, because nobody re-reads a deleted file. Every removal names the search that found nothing.

SCOPE NOTE: this repo is specification plus skeletons and **nothing moves bytes yet**. 'Dead code' here means scaffolding that no longer matches the spec it was written against, not unreachable runtime paths — there is barely a runtime. Be correspondingly careful: a skeleton is not dead because it is unused.

PAIRED WITH THE DOCS SWEEP, WHICH RUNS AFTER. Removing code changes what the docs should say, so the docs tasklist depends on this one. Do not fix docs here beyond what a removal strands.

userStories.title: An inventory, measured before anything is removed
userStories.notes: Verify green for everything that could run: .chief/verify.sh 3 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed — PASS Swift build, PASS Swift tests (46 passed: 4 upload-path, 39 state-machine vectors, 3 I6 transport vectors), PASS TypeScript typecheck, SKIPPED Gradle build (no JDK on PATH, so UNVERIFIED not passed). Also ran the four cheap CI gates directly: check-single-fixture.sh PASS ("one fixture at Tests/Conformance/vectors.json, referenced by both ports"), verify-skip-policy.sh "all assertions passed", check:control-surface "spec remains control-surface only", drift-control.sh --port swift "2 controls ran, 0 skipped, 0 failures". Docs-only change touching no Kotlin, so the Gradle skip strands nothing in this story. ARTIFACT: docs/reference/dead-code-inventory.md (289 lines), indexed in docs/README.md. NINE SEARCHES, each named with its command and scope (S1-S9): per-type and per-function reference counts over all 54 Swift types / 84 Kotlin types / every function in both ports; a 6-normalised-line duplicate-block hash per language; commented-out-code and TODO scans; per-dependency import counts; version-guard vs minSdk/platforms comparison; and a per-script grep against ci.yml and verify.sh. FINDINGS. Genuinely dead, 6: resume_data is a write-only table (storeResumeData called at DefaultUploadEngine.swift:298, loadResumeData has 0 call sites and 0 mentions in docs/Tests/packages/integration); UploadDao.inState:22 (1 grep hit, its own declaration, and no Swift counterpart); WireDialect.Rufh Kotlin:62-91 (the ONLY type in either port with refcount 0 — every construction site passes Tus10, and vectors.json has 0 occurrences of dialect/Upload-Draft/partial-upload); androidx.core:core-ktx (0 `^import androidx.core` hits vs 8 room / 5 work / 19 coroutines / 13 okhttp3); UploadNotifications.kt:31 SDK_INT >= O against minSdk 26, condition can never be false; three redundant @RequiresApi(O) in StorageGovernor.kt. Deliberately unexercised, 8, NOT to be deleted: the ten EnumConverters @TypeConverter methods all report 0 call sites and the module cannot compile without them (kapt emits the calls, and kapt runs nowhere on this machine); renewLease/pruneCompleted uncalled in BOTH ports symmetrically and carrying a stated retention policy plus half of invariant I8; Swift SourceResolver.stageIfRequired:62 has 0 callers while its Kotlin twin is called at DefaultUploadEngine.kt:217 — the caller is missing, not the callee, and that is port drift not dead code; the nativeResumeUnavailable chain across 5 files whose terminal operation is a set-remove on a set never inserted into and never read, kept because wire-protocol.md:57-63 specifies the behaviour it is the skeleton of; consumer-rules.pro; the RN control surface (external consumers); the tusd harness (docs state why it is not in CI). Duplicated implementations, 3, ranked by drift cost: the six-arm HTTP-status-to-ErrorClass table written out VERBATIM twice in Swift at BackgroundSessionManager.swift:212-223 and ControlPlaneClient.swift:124-132, read on two different code paths and covered by no vector — worst of the three; the two Swift transports sharing 9 overlapping 6-line windows (create/head/terminate delegations plus the whole PATCH construction); and the .offsetAdvanced prefix duplicated at UploadStateMachine.swift:86-92 and :156-169. Kotlin had ZERO duplicate blocks. Undecidable, 4 classes, left in place: cross-repo consumers, kapt codegen, framework dispatch (URLSession/ConnectivityManager/OkHttp/WorkManager callbacks all report 0 call sites and are all mandatory), and reflection — searched for Class.forName/NSClassFromString/dynamicMemberLookup and found none. Two negatives worth recording: 0 commented-out code blocks in any source language, 0 unused Swift imports, and exactly one TODO (StorageGovernor.kt:97) which names future work rather than hiding an abandoned path.
acceptanceCriteria: Produce a checked-in inventory of candidates with, for each, the SEARCH that found it unreferenced — the command and its scope. A candidate list without its method is unreviewable, and this is the artifact a human approves before deletion.
Separate genuinely-dead from deliberately-unexercised. The second class exists here on purpose (refusal paths, guards, unreached tiers that say so) and deleting it removes a stated contract.
Include duplicated implementations as first-class findings, not just unused ones — two implementations of one behaviour is the failure mode that costs most later, because they drift.
GATES: the repo's own verify green.

userStories.title: Removal, with the tree still green and the reason recorded
userStories.notes: GATES after every one of the four commits: .chief/verify.sh -> 3 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed (PASS Swift build, PASS Swift tests 46 passed, PASS TypeScript typecheck, SKIPPED Gradle build - no JDK on PATH, so UNVERIFIED not passed). Per CLAUDE.md SS3 that is NOT green, and it matters here: three of the four removals are Kotlin and rest entirely on CI. All four cheap CI gates green on the final tree: check-single-fixture.sh "one fixture at Tests/Conformance/vectors.json, referenced by both ports"; verify-skip-policy.sh "all assertions passed"; check:control-surface "spec remains control-surface only"; drift-control.sh --port swift "2 controls ran, 0 skipped, 0 failures". REVIEWABLE STEPS - four commits, one finding each, each independently revertable: afabf05 (SS3.1 dedupe), ac91b10 (SS1.2 UploadDao.inState + its stranded UploadState import), 9edd129 (SS1.5 the SDK_INT >= O guard), 6d16ac7 (SS1.4 the androidx.core:core-ktx declaration). NO TEST WAS DELETED, WEAKENED OR ADJUSTED to keep anything green - the Swift suite runs the same 46 cases before and after (4 upload-path, 39 state-machine vectors, 3 I6 transport vectors), and no Kotlin test referenced any of the three Kotlin rows. THE MOST VALUABLE COMMIT IS afabf05: TransportError.errorClass restated HTTPStatus.classify's six-arm table verbatim, read on two different code paths, covered by no vector - editing one copy would have shipped a build that retries 429 on HEAD and gives up on it mid-transfer with all 40 vectors passing. One table now, with a comment at HTTPStatus.classify saying why it is the only copy. THREE OF THE SIX SS1 CANDIDATES WERE NOT REMOVED, each recorded with why. (1) loadResumeData: the inventory's corroboration row was FACTUALLY WRONG. It claimed the grep over docs/ Tests/ packages/ integration/ 'returns nothing'; re-running it verbatim returns four lines - ios-background-transfer.md:65-66 ('we persist the blob BEFORE reporting the error, since its presence means resumable rather than start over') and platform-constraints.md:21-22, which names the consumer uploadTask(withResumeData:). So the function is the unimplemented READ half of a specified iOS 17 capability, the same shape as SS2.4's nativeResumeUnavailable chain, and belongs in SS2. The disk leak the inventory flagged is real and unchanged - it is a defect to fix by implementing the reader, not by deleting it. (2) WireDialect.Rufh (Kotlin): wire-protocol.md:5-9 opens 'Two dialects, one transport interface' with a column-per-dialect table naming Rufh beside Tus10, written to span both ports, and Swift's RufhDialect is live at UploadTransport.swift:64. Deleting the Kotlin half makes a documented two-dialect seam single-dialect on one platform. Needs a decision (implement the construction site, or amend the doc to say RUFH is iOS-only), not a sweep. (3) The three @RequiresApi(O): true documentation - getAllocatableBytes/allocateBytes did arrive in API 26 - and the sole reason androidx.annotation is on the classpath, so removing them strands a second dependency for no behavioural gain. DUPLICATIONS SS3.2 and SS3.3 deferred with reasons: the two-transport pair crosses exactly the seam invariant I6's three transport vectors watch (and the difference between the transports IS I6), and .offsetAdvanced is a shared six-line prefix of state-machine policy pinned by all 40 vectors - lowest severity, highest risk. ARTIFACT: docs/reference/dead-code-removal.md, indexed in docs/README.md; the inventory's acted-on rows carry REMOVED/NOT REMOVED/SUPERSEDED markers pointing at it, and its SS1.1 corroboration and judgement rows are struck through in place rather than silently rewritten. CHANGELOG.md gains a 2026-09-03 entry marking each Kotlin removal 'verified in CI only'.
acceptanceCriteria: Remove what US-1 established, in reviewable steps rather than one sweep. A single commit deleting hundreds of lines across unrelated subsystems cannot be reviewed and cannot be partially reverted.
The full gate passes after each step. A removal that needs a test deleted to stay green is a removal of something live — say so and stop rather than adjusting the test.
Anything NOT removed that looked dead is recorded with why it survived. That record is worth more than the deletions: it is what stops the next sweep re-litigating the same files.
GATES: the repo's own verify green.

userStories.title: What the sweep could not decide
userStories.notes: GATES: .chief/verify.sh -> 3 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed (PASS Swift build, PASS Swift tests 46 passed [4 upload-path, 39 state-machine vectors, 3 I6 transport vectors], PASS TypeScript typecheck, SKIPPED Gradle build - no JDK on PATH, so UNVERIFIED not passed per CLAUDE.md SS3). All four cheap CI gates green: check-single-fixture.sh "one fixture at Tests/Conformance/vectors.json, referenced by both ports"; verify-skip-policy.sh "all assertions passed"; check:control-surface "spec remains control-surface only"; drift-control.sh --port swift "2 controls ran, 0 skipped, 0 failures". Docs-only change; `git status` confirms no file under ios/ android/ packages/ differs from HEAD. ARTIFACT: docs/reference/dead-code-undecidable.md, indexed in docs/README.md, cross-linked from both prior artifacts. NOTHING REMOVED - the deliverable is the register. SIX BLIND-SPOT CLASSES, where the inventory's SS4 named four; the two it missed both occur here. (1.1) Consumers outside the repo: AmphoraUploader.configure and .handleBackgroundEvents return 1 grep line each - their own declaration; `grep -rn AmphoraUploader ios/` returns 2 lines total, both in the file that declares it; Kotlin AmphoraUploader.get is referenced only inside its own companion. Applied honestly to the top of this library, S1/S3 report THE ENTIRE PUBLIC API OF BOTH PORTS AS DEAD - the searches that produced the inventory would delete the library. The consumer is a Markdown fence in ios-host-integration.md, which calls both and labels them "Not optional". Plus 10 named RN exports with 0 in-repo importers. (1.2) Codegen: 10 @TypeConverters, UploadDatabase.uploads(), 12 DAO bodies, AmphoraSpec (found by Native*.ts FILENAME convention, not by import). (1.3) Framework dispatch: 4 URLSession delegate methods, 3 ConnectivityManager callbacks, 2 OkHttp callbacks, doWork, 4 RangeRequestBody members, close(), and the UploadWorker constructor. didReceiveInformationalResponse is not merely uncalled but UNCALLABLE by anything this repo can run. (1.4) Reflection - the inventory's answer was TRUE AND MISLEADING: this tree has no Class.forName, because the reflection that reaches this code lives in Room (UploadDatabase::class.java -> UploadDatabase_Impl by name), WorkManager (worker class name persisted into a row) and TurboModuleRegistry.getEnforcing('Amphora'). Searching this tree for reflection can only ever return zero. (1.5) NEW CLASS - symbols bound by string, not by reference. THE PROOF, AND IT IS A CONTROL EXPERIMENT NOT AN ASSERTION: BlockReason.powerLow has ZERO references in BOTH ports - by the inventory's own reasoning (SS1.3, WireDialect.Rufh) the strongest dead signal this repo offers. Commenting the case out and rebuilding: `swift build` -> "Build complete! (3.45s)", i.e. COMPILES CLEAN; `swift run AmphoraPathTests` -> "ConformanceTests.swift:165: Fatal error: Unexpectedly found nil". Restored, 46 passed, git confirms the file is byte-identical to HEAD. Exactly one of the 40 vectors (row-14-power-low) reaches it, by raw-value decode; expect.blockReason is asserted by neither runner. Also 4 enum-to-SQL contracts (UploadState raw values spelled into SQL literals at SQLiteUploadStore.swift:53/57/61/139 and UploadDao.kt:17/21/54) and 6 identity strings. (1.6) NEW CLASS - edges existing only across a process boundary: taskDescription written before termination and read after OS-initiated relaunch, the whole Reconciler adopt path, systemCompletionHandler (BOTH of whose ends are already undecidable), and resume_data. Invisible to grep AND to the local suite - the same gap ROADMAP.md records as 40 unverified device cells. A DEFECT FOUND BY READING THE ROWS RATHER THAN COUNTING THEM, reported not fixed: UploadWorker.kt:84 tags work "amphora-job:$jobId" and its two addTag calls at :92/:114 are the ONLY ones in the module, while Reconciler.kt:111 queries the exact tag "amphora-job" (:120). getWorkInfosByTag matches by string EQUALITY, not prefix, so liveWorkJobIds() returns an empty set on every launch and the Android adopt path can never fire. Corroboration that the two ends disagree: :113 strips the "amphora-job:" prefix off results the query cannot have returned. No test covers it (grep over android/src/test returns nothing); unverified locally - no JDK, and it needs an instrumented device regardless. Third defect this tasklist surfaced without fixing, after the missing stageIfRequired call and the write-only resume_data table. LIMITS OF THE METHOD stated as SS3, seven items, incl. the one this tasklist learned expensively: a QUOTED search reads exactly like an EXECUTED one - which is why powerLow was verified by running the deletion rather than by reasoning about it. CORRECTIONS TO PRIOR ARTIFACTS, struck through in place per the US-2 precedent rather than silently rewritten: inventory SS4's four-class list is marked incomplete (four -> six, three occur -> five occur), SS4.4's reflection finding is struck and corrected, and the SS5 summary row now reads "4 classes as measured, 6 on review". CHANGELOG.md gains Added + Changed entries for 2026-09-03.
acceptanceCriteria: Report candidates the sweep could not resolve — reachable only through dynamic dispatch, reflection, generated code, or a consumer outside this repo — and leave them in place. An honest 'undecidable' list is a legitimate result.
State the limits of the method: what a static search over this tree cannot see. Cross-repo consumers are the obvious one, and this portfolio has already been bitten by exactly that.
GATES: the repo's own verify green.
